title: The ECJ Whisperer
description: The Court of Justice of the European Union does not operate through a strict hierarchy of Treaty, secondary law, and national law. Instead, once a competence is triggered, the Court treats secondary law as a self-contained system, unless a claimant identifies a precise error in conferral. Its judgments test for localised coherence rather than institutional balance, which leads to continuous expansion of EU law. Member States, lacking procedural tools to defend retained competences, risk structural erosion of sovereignty. This paper explains that method, and proposes a counter-structure: the Inland Security Infrastructure Act to Protect Human Dignity (ISIG-ZUM). ISIG-ZUM is presented as a thought experiment, showing how national law might evolve in structural symmetry with EU law to preserve the balance of competences envisaged by the Treaties.
